record.paper_title: On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems
record.original_question: Defineν w =S w(1, . . . ,1) which is the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomialS w of the permutationw. For a givenn, defineu(n) to be the maximumν w forw ∈ S_n. For a given n, what permutationsw ∈ S_n maximizeν w? Asn→ ∞, is there some kind of “limiting shape” of the permutationsw ∈ S_n for whichν w =u(n)?

For a givenn, defineu(n) to be the maximumν w forw∈S n. For a given n, what permutationsw∈S n maximizeν w? Asn→ ∞, is there some kind of “limiting shape” of the permutationsw∈S n for whichν w =u(n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a permutation $w \in S_n$, let $\mathfrak{S}_w(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n-1}) \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_{n-1}]$ denote the Schubert polynomial of $w$, defined recursively by $\mathfrak{S}_{w_0} = x_1^{n-1} x_2^{n-2} \cdots x_{n-1}$ for the longest permutation $w_0 \in S_n$, and $\mathfrak{S}_{w s_i} = \partial_i \mathfrak{S}_w$ whenever $\ell(w s_i) < \ell(w)$, where $s_i = (i, i+1)$ and $\partial_i f = (f - s_i f)/(x_i - x_{i+1})$ is the divided difference operator. Define the principal specialization at $1$:
$$\nu_w := \mathfrak{S}_w(1, 1, \ldots, 1),$$
which equals the sum of all coefficients of $\mathfrak{S}_w$. For each positive integer $n$, set
$$u(n) := \max_{w \in S_n} \nu_w.$$

(a) For each $n$, determine all permutations $w \in S_n$ that achieve $\nu_w = u(n)$.

(b) Determine whether, as $n \to \infty$, the maximizing permutations $w \in S_n$ (suitably rescaled, viewed as permutation matrices in $[0,1]^2$) admit a limit shape, and if so describe it explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is associated with a conjecture of Merzon–Smirnov (2014) asserting that maximizers are layered permutations; Stanley posed the asymptotic/limit-shape question. Morales–Pak–Panova (2018, "Asymptotics of principal evaluations of Schubert polynomials for layered permutations") resolved Stanley's questions restricted to layered permutations and proved a limit shape there, but the underlying Merzon–Smirnov conjecture identifying all maximizers as layered remains open. Hence the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics of principal evaluations of Schubert polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Morales, Pak, Panova resolve Stanley's problems on u(n) and limit shape restricted to layered permutations.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic and limit-shape questions are resolved conditionally on, or restricted to, layered permutations.

status_evidence.title: Principal specializations of Schubert polynomials and pattern containment
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Merzon–Smirnov conjecture that maximizers of principal specialization are layered permutations.
status_evidence.claim: The Merzon–Smirnov conjecture identifying maximizers as layered permutations remains open.
